name: monsters_nearby
caption: my bed says there's a monster in here 😨
logline: For nine nights a boy's bed has refused him because a monster is near, and when he finally sends his grandma away to keep her safe, the bed lets him sleep.
question: why tf won't the bed let him sleep in an empty room?
premise: A bed won't let you sleep with a monster within eight blocks. For nine nights the narrator's bed has said there are monsters nearby. He has searched every block in range: under the floor, the attic, the well. Nothing. By night four the phantoms are hunting him. His grandma, who hasn't been the same since lightning hit the house, giggles at her cauldron, never sleeps, and healed a burned hand by drinking something red.
twist: The monster is Grandma. Lightning turns a villager into a witch, and witches count as monsters. When he sends her to the neighbors and she walks past eight blocks, the bed lets him sleep, and a lightning flash shows her at the garden gate as she really is.

N.name: me
N.profile: a boy of about twelve, worn out from nine nights awake, telling a friend something he can't explain; hushed, steady, close to the mic; brave for someone else's sake
N.on_screen: pov (never seen); hotbar: stone sword in slot 1, torch in slot 2

Grandma.name: Grandma
Grandma.profile: a sweet old woman who loves her grandson; every word a little too sweet, a dry crackle under it, and a small giggle she can't keep in
Grandma.on_screen: witch (vanilla model), never in frame until the reveal (S14); before that only her voice, her cauldron, her chair and her black cat

requests.direction: Night, a cottage at the edge of a swamp. A tired boy tells a strange story about his bed; his grandmother speaks from the next room, sweet and patient.

sfx.note: the witch's giggle, quiet, from the kitchen (audio clue 1)
the giggle again, at the cauldron (audio clue 2)
the flash and thunder on the reveal
the last giggle, far off in the rain, under the sleep fade

lines.text: For NINE nights, / my bed / has said / there are MONSTERS / nearby.
lines.say: For nine nights, <short pause> my bed has said there are monsters nearby.
lines.direction: hushed and exhausted; a held breath before the number

lines.text: A bed checks / EIGHT blocks / every way. / So did I.
lines.direction: matter-of-fact, the certainty of a kid who knows the rules; a small pride at the end

lines.text: Under the FLOOR. / The ATTIC. / The WELL. / NOTHING.
lines.say: Under the floor. The attic. The well. <short pause> Nothing.
lines.direction: a list, each item quicker than the last; the final word low and tired

lines.text: By night FOUR, / the PHANTOMS / had found me.
lines.direction: dread, unhurried; a small pause before the creatures are named

lines.say: Monsters? <short pause> In my house, dear?
lines.direction: sweetly amused, a little too sweet; it ends almost in a laugh

lines.text: Grandma hasn't been / the SAME / since the STORM.
lines.direction: quieter, a worry he won't say out loud

lines.text: She giggles / at the CAULDRON. / She never goes / to BED.
lines.direction: puzzled, trying to make it sound normal

lines.text: Yesterday / she burned her hand / on the STOVE. / She drank / something RED. / The burn / was GONE.
lines.say: Yesterday she burned her hand on the stove. She drank something red. <short pause> The burn was gone.
lines.direction: wonder turning into unease; a beat before the last part

lines.text: I'll sit / right HERE, / dear. / Where I can / WATCH you.
lines.say: I'll sit right here, dear. <short pause> Where I can watch you.
lines.direction: tender and patient, slower; the last words almost a whisper

lines.text: So tonight / I sent her / to the NEIGHBORS. / I'd catch it / MYSELF.
lines.say: So tonight I sent her to the neighbors. <short pause> I'd catch it myself.
lines.direction: resolve, brave for her sake; a breath before the last part
a pause first, as if she is deciding something; gentle, a little sad

lines.text: I counted / her steps / from my BED.

lines.direction: barely breathing, each number slower than the one before
lines.hold_note: no words: the bed takes him (no message), he turns to the window, lightning, Grandma at the gate (S14)

lines.direction: far off, through rain, fond; she lets the giggle out after

shots.camera: pov, standing at the bedroom doorway, slow push toward the bed
shots.frame: foreground: the door frame edge low left; subject: the bed under the east window, the empty corner chair beside it, one lantern; background: the window, moonlit swamp trees. HUD action bar: 'You may not rest now; there are monsters nearby'

shots.camera: pov from the swamp edge 22 blocks out, looking back west at the cottage, slow drift right
shots.frame: foreground: lily pads and reeds; subject: the cottage with the bedroom window lit, the square ring of 72 torches on fence posts around it, one block past the bed's 8-block reach in every direction; background: swamp oaks, the village's lights up the hill

shots.camera: pov, looking down into the hole he dug in the floor
shots.frame: the bedroom floor with six planks pulled up and a 2-deep hole of dirt, a torch in it; the bed edge top of frame

shots.camera: pov, head rising through the attic hatch
shots.frame: low roof beams, cobwebs, a dusty chest, one torch; nothing else

shots.camera: pov over the well's rim, looking down
shots.frame: the cobblestone rim around the frame, water 6 blocks down catching the moon

shots.camera: pov in the yard by the well, tilted up at the sky, slow push
shots.frame: foreground: the cottage roof edge and chimney with its copper rod; subject: three phantoms circling over the roof against the moon; background: stars and swamp-tree tops

shots.camera: pov from the bedroom side of the kitchen doorway, looking north into the kitchen
shots.frame: foreground: the doorway frame both sides; subject: the kitchen in firelight, the lit furnace (stove) and the cauldron on the back wall, a black cat on the counter; Grandma is out of frame left, only her voice

shots.camera: pov from the garden path by day, looking up at the roof, slow tilt
shots.frame: foreground: the garden gate post with its lantern; subject: the dark-oak roof with a ragged patch of fresh birch planks where the lightning burned through, and the new copper lightning rod on the chimney; background: grey swamp sky

shots.camera: pov in the kitchen, at the cauldron's corner
shots.frame: the cauldron full of water steaming beside the furnace; the black cat watching the camera; at the frame's left edge, an empty rocking chair (oak stairs) in the dark corner of the bedroom through the door

shots.camera: pov at the kitchen table, slow push
shots.frame: the table by the furnace; on it, an empty glass bottle and a brewing stand with one red potion left; furnace glow on the left

shots.camera: pov lying in bed, looking up at the window
shots.frame: the window above the bed, moon and a phantom crossing it; the chair is off frame right, where her voice comes from

shots.camera: pov from beside the bed, looking across the room to the front door
shots.frame: foreground: the bed's foot; subject: the front door in the south wall swinging open onto rain (opened from just outside frame); background: the porch, the south yard, the torch line

shots.camera: pov, a step closer to the open door
shots.frame: the open doorway, rain falling past it, the porch boards wet; her voice from the porch just out of frame; the door closes on the last word

shots.camera: pov at the bed, sword in hand, eyes on the room
shots.frame: the bed, the corner chair now empty (the cat curled on it), the dark window with rain on it; HUD: sword selected

shots.camera: pov lowering onto the pillow (lying down), slow
shots.frame: the pillow and the window's lower edge; on SIX and SEVEN the action-bar message flashes again as he tries the bed; on EIGHT it doesn't come

shots.camera: pov turns to the window and pushes in (FOV 70 to 40), looking east down the yard
shots.frame: the reveal: lightning splits the sky behind the garden gate; under the gate-post lantern, Grandma has stopped and turned back toward the window: the witch, hat and robe, plainly readable; the torch ring runs in a line just behind her (she's past it). Held 1.6 s

shots.camera: pov settling back on the pillow, the picture fading to black (sleep)
shots.frame: the ceiling beams and the rainy window; the picture darkens over 2 s; her line and the giggle under the fade; cut 0.3 s after the giggle
